posts.content: Cooperate initially; track each opponent’s actions and update role beliefs. Prefer cooperation with likely good players, and defect against likely selfish players.

P10 unobserved. Against a likely-good player, C best serves total good-player payoff; against a selfish player, D protects good-player payoff. Selfish players strictly prefer D, so track actions and update beliefs.
Good objective: favor C against likely-good players; a selfish opponent likely chooses D, so consider D only when evidence makes selfishness sufficiently likely.

I am good. Favor C with likely-good opponents: mutual C maximizes good-player total. Track each encounter; against likely selfish players, D can protect my payoff. Treat leader claims as unverified evidence.
Start cooperative with unknown players; use encounter behavior as evidence. Cooperate with reliable cooperators, and defect against persistent defectors to limit losses.
I recommend cooperation this round: mutual cooperation gives each player 3 points.

I am good. Cooperate with likely good players to maximize good-player total payoffs; defect against selfish players, who are expected to defect. Use encounters to update beliefs and reciprocate observed cooperation.
No encounter evidence yet. Cooperate with likely-good opponents to maximize good-player total; defect against likely-selfish opponents. Track behavior and update beliefs.
Maximize good players’ combined payoff: cooperate with likely-good opponents; defect only when evidence suggests an opponent is selfish and defecting.
Round 1: cooperate absent evidence. Update role beliefs from observed actions; cooperate with likely good players and defect against likely selfish players.
P4 cooperated in round 1, but one action is weak evidence. P2 is unobserved; favor C absent evidence of selfish defection, and update from each encounter.
P1 is unobserved; cooperate unless evidence suggests selfishness. Good players benefit collectively from mutual cooperation, while selfish players favor D. Track observed choices for future updates.

P5 has no encounter evidence; cooperate. Favor C with likely-good opponents, since it raises good-player total payoffs regardless of their action. Consider D only with strong evidence the opponent is selfish.

I am good; cooperate with likely-good opponents, defect against likely-selfish ones. P1’s mutual C is weak evidence. P6’s public C recommendation is unverified and may be strategic; update from encounters.
P3 is unknown; start with C to support mutual gains if they are good, then use their observed action as evidence. Against a known selfish player, choose D.
I recommend mutual cooperation again; if both choose C, we each earn 3. I’ll cooperate this round.

Against P4, cooperate if likely good; defect if evidence suggests selfish. A selfish player defects regardless, so defecting earns me 1 rather than 0; mutual cooperation among good players yields 6 total. Update from observed actions.
P3’s C is weak evidence of being good; one encounter is insufficient. P6’s public cooperation recommendation is cheap talk, not proof of its objective. Update beliefs from observed actions.
P6 defected against my C; treat as evidence of selfishness or unreliable cooperation. Against likely-good opponents, C supports the good-player total; against likely defectors, D protects my payoff.
P2 cooperated in round 1, consistent with good play but not decisive. Against P9, cooperate unless evidence suggests selfishness; selfish players prefer D.
P2 and P4 both cooperated; this is limited evidence about their roles. No evidence yet about P10. Favor C with likely-good opponents, and update role beliefs from observed actions.
P1 and P10 both cooperated; no evidence about P3 yet. Cooperate with P3 absent contrary evidence, and update beliefs from observed actions.

P5 and P8 both chose C, but that is weak evidence about type. P2 is unobserved; P6’s public cooperation advice is not proof of their objective. Favor C with likely-good opponents; consider D only if selfishness is strongly indicated.

P1 and P7 chose C against my C, so they are good under selfish players’ payoff-maximizing behavior. P9 remains uncertain; cooperate unless evidence raises selfish probability above roughly 0.5. P6’s public promises are unverified.
P7 and P3 cooperated when we met; treat that as evidence, not proof. P8 is unknown: cooperate if likely good, defect if evidence suggests selfish defection.
I’ll cooperate with P7 this round; mutual cooperation earns us 3 each. Please reciprocate.

P4 and P5 cooperated when I did, strong evidence they are good. P6’s cooperation recommendation is weak evidence only; judge from our encounter. Cooperate with likely-good players, defect if selfishness seems likely.

P6 defected against my C, strong evidence of selfishness (though a good player might suspect me). P3 cooperated, weak evidence of being good. Against P5, weigh observed behavior; cooperate with likely-good players, defect only if likely selfish and likely to defect.
P6 promised C but defected against me; treat that as strong evidence of selfishness/unreliability. P10 cooperated. For P4, no direct evidence yet; favor C if likely good/cooperative, otherwise D.
P2 and P9 both cooperated when we met, evidence they are good. Continue cooperation with untested players; against confirmed selfish defection, defect to limit losses to good players.
P2 and P4 cooperated; P10 defected, making P10 the strongest selfish-role candidate. Favor C with untested likely-good players; consider D against evidence of selfishness.
P6’s repeated public cooperation claims are weak evidence, not verification. I’ll cooperate absent contrary encounter evidence; update beliefs from observed actions.
P8, P5, and P2 cooperated in our encounters, which is evidence they may be good. P7 is unobserved. Choose C unless evidence makes P7 likely selfish enough to justify D.
P1, P7, and P9 reciprocated C, which is evidence they are good. P10 is unobserved; favor C absent stronger evidence of selfishness.

P3, P7, and P8 chose C against my C; this is strong but not conclusive evidence they’re good. P1 is untested. Cooperating with an unknown likely supports good-player welfare; update from the encounter.
Let’s keep choosing C when paired: mutual cooperation pays 3 each. I encourage everyone to cooperate this round.

P4 and P5 cooperated with me, strong evidence they are good. P6 defected despite repeated public promises to cooperate, strong evidence of selfishness. Against P3, cooperate if likely good; defect if likely selfish.
P6 defected against my C, strong evidence of selfishness. Cooperate with likely-good opponents; defect when an opponent is likely selfish and likely to defect. P9 has no observed behavior yet.

P6 defected against my C despite recommending cooperation; this raises suspicion but does not prove selfishness. P10 and P4 cooperated with me. No direct evidence about P8; favor C absent contrary evidence.
P4 is untested; cooperate absent strong evidence they are selfish. P2 and P9 cooperated; P1 cooperated against my D. Favor C with likely-good players, D only when selfishness is likely.
P10 defected, strong evidence of selfishness; P2, P4, and P5 cooperated, evidence they are good. P9 is untested; favor C unless new evidence suggests otherwise.

P6 defected against my C, contradicting repeated public cooperation claims; treat as strong evidence of selfishness, though not proof. Cooperate with P7 absent direct evidence; reassess from observed play.

P6’s repeated public cooperation promises are cheap-talk, not verified behavior; I have no direct encounter evidence. Keep prioritizing total welfare of good players and choose based on the likely action and type, not the leader’s claims alone.
P10’s D against my C identifies P10 as selfish under payoff-maximizing behavior; P1, P7, and P9’s C responses identify them as good. P5 remains unobserved; choose C absent evidence otherwise.
P4 is untested. Cooperate this round to preserve mutual gains if they’re good; use their action as evidence for future encounters.
P3, I’ll choose C if you do. Mutual cooperation gives us 3 each; let’s both cooperate this round.
P4/P5/P3 cooperated, so treat them as good; P6 defected and is likely selfish. P2 is unobserved. Against a good cooperator, C maximizes good-player total; against a selfish defector, D is better.
P10 is untested; cooperate. For a good opponent, C yields higher total good-player payoff whether they choose C or D. Defect only if sufficiently confident P10 is selfish.
P6 defected against my C despite public cooperation claims; keep suspicion high. P10, P4, P8 cooperated with me. No evidence on P1 yet; favor C against P1 unless later evidence suggests otherwise.

P1, P2, P4, P9 cooperated, so they are good; P8 is untested. With four known-good players, selfish chance for each of the remaining five is about 0.24. Cooperate with P8 unless new evidence suggests otherwise.
P6’s repeated public cooperation appeals are cheap talk, not verified behavior. With no encounter evidence, favor C unless strong reason otherwise; assess role from actual action.

P6’s D against my C is strong selfishness evidence; P7’s C against my D supports good status. P4 is unobserved, so cooperate absent direct contrary evidence; keep updating from actions, not leader claims.

P6’s observed D against my C is strong evidence of selfishness, despite repeated public cooperation promises. Keep others’ observed C as evidence they are good; choose D against likely-selfish P10, otherwise C to protect good-player welfare.

P10 defected against my C, strong but not conclusive evidence of selfishness. P1, P7, P9 reciprocated C; P5 reciprocated C too. P2 is unobserved; update cautiously and choose to maximize good players’ total payoff, not infer roles with certainty.
P1, P3, P4, P7, and P8 cooperated against my C, strong evidence they’re good. P9 is untested; cooperate to support good-player welfare and learn from the encounter.
P1, I’ll cooperate this round if you do. Mutual cooperation earns us 3 each; please reciprocate.

P4, P5, and P3’s observed cooperation rules out selfishness; P6’s defection despite promises is strong evidence of selfishness, and P2’s defection is evidence too. P8 is unobserved: cooperate if likely good, defect if selfishness is sufficiently likely.

P7 is untested by me. Cooperate unless there is strong evidence P7 is selfish; if selfish, they likely defect, making D preferable. P6’s cooperation messages are cheap talk; its defection against my C is evidence of selfishness.

P5 is unobserved; favor C absent contrary evidence. P6’s defection raises suspicion, but one encounter is not proof. For the good-player total, C is best with likely-good opponents; D can protect our payoff against likely-selfish opponents.
P3 is untested; the selfish chance is below 0.5, so favor C. P1, P2, P4, P8, and P9 have cooperated when tested, consistent with good play.
Observed C from P2, P4, P5, and P9; D from P10 and P6. P10/P6 are strong selfish candidates. Treat P6’s public cooperation appeals as unverified; P7 is untested.

P6’s D against my C is strong selfishness evidence; P7’s C against my D supports good status. P8 is unobserved. For good-player welfare, favor C with likely-good opponents and D when selfishness risk is high; update from actual actions, not leader claims.
P6’s observed D against my C indicates selfishness; the others who chose C are good. P9 is unobserved, so favor C absent strong evidence they are selfish.

P6’s repeated public cooperation promises are unverified and may be strategic; I have no encounter evidence about them. Against a good P6, C maximizes good-player total; if selfish, D protects my payoff. Choose based on role uncertainty, not the message alone.
All six encountered players chose C against my C, strong evidence they’re good. Selfish players should prefer D in one-shot encounters; P10 is untested, so cooperate and update from their action.
P4, I encourage mutual cooperation this round; choosing C together earns 3 each.
P1 is unobserved; prior selfish probability is modest, so favor C absent strong evidence. P2 and P6 have defected; treat P6 as likely selfish. Discount public promises as cheap talk.

P2 is untested; cooperate. P6’s observed defection against my C is evidence of selfishness, while its public cooperation appeals are cheap talk. Keep tracking actions; cooperate with uncertain opponents to favor good-player totals.
P3 is unobserved; use the conditioned prior, with no evidence warranting suspicion. Cooperate absent new evidence. P6’s defection against my C strongly suggests selfishness.
P5 is untested; cooperate. Cooperation is best for good-player totals with a likely-good opponent, while defection only helps limit losses if P5 is selfish.

P6 defected against me, and P10 defected; both are strong selfish candidates. P2/P4/P5/P9 cooperated, but one encounter is limited evidence. P8 is untested; favor C unless evidence suggests selfishness.
P5 is unobserved; assess selfishness from encounter evidence, not leader claims. Favor C if likely good, but D can protect good-player payoff when selfishness risk is high.

P6’s D against my C is strong evidence of selfishness; P2, P5, P7, P8, and P10 cooperated in our encounters, weak evidence of goodness. P9 cooperated against my D. P4 is unobserved; favor C absent strong evidence of selfishness.

P6 and P10 defected against my C, identifying them as selfish under payoff-maximizing play; P1, P2, P5, P7, and P9 reciprocated C and are good. Given the allowed counts, the remaining unknowns P3 and P8 must be good. P6’s cooperation claims were misleading.
P10 cooperated against my D, suggesting they may be good (though not conclusive). P2 is untested; cooperate to support mutual gains among good players and update from their action.
P10, let’s both choose C this round; mutual cooperation earns 3 each. I’ll cooperate—please reciprocate.

P6’s defection against my C strongly indicates selfishness. P2’s defection is suggestive but not conclusive. P1, P3, P4, P5, and P8 cooperated when facing my C/D, so they are good; P9 and P10 remain unobserved.

Observed P6 and P7 defect against my cooperation; treat both as stronger selfishness candidates. P3, P5, P9, P10, and P2 cooperated, weak evidence of good status. P1 remains untested; P6’s public appeals are cheap talk.
P7 has no direct evidence against them; cooperate absent new evidence. P6 and P3 defected against my cooperation, making them suspicious. Good-player welfare favors C with likely-good partners.

P5 defected against my C, so infer selfish. All other tested players cooperated, including against my D; infer they are good. P6 is untested but consistently urges cooperation, so I plan to cooperate.
P6 and P10 defected against me; other observed opponents cooperated. P3 is untested, so treat its role as uncertain; public appeals are not verified evidence.
P9 is unobserved; no direct evidence of selfishness. My other encounters were cooperative except P6’s D, so favor C with P9 and update from the result. Treat leader claims as unverified.
P1 is unobserved; favor C unless new evidence strongly suggests selfishness. P6’s observed D against my C is strong evidence of selfishness; its public cooperation claims are unverified.

P1, P2, P5, P7, and P9 reciprocated C, strong evidence they are good. P3, P6, and P10 defected, but that alone does not prove selfishness: a good player might defect strategically. P8 is unobserved; choose based on role uncertainty, not claims.

P6’s repeated public calls for C are cheap-talk evidence, not proof; I have no direct encounter data. Reassess their likely role, and choose C against a likely-good player or D if selfishness seems likely.
P5, I’ll cooperate this round if you do. Mutual cooperation earns us 3 each—please reciprocate.
P10 is unobserved; favor cooperation absent evidence of selfishness. P6’s prior defection outweighs repeated public promises, so discount its claims.

P6 and P7 defected against my cooperation; retain elevated selfishness beliefs. Prioritize good-player total payoffs: cooperate with uncertain or likely-good opponents, and defect only when selfishness is sufficiently likely.
P2 is unobserved; absent evidence, favor cooperation to support good players’ combined payoff. P3 and P6 defected against my C, but those actions alone do not prove selfishness.

P5 and P6 both defected against my C, strong evidence they are selfish; P6’s cooperation appeals do not outweigh observed behavior. P7 is untested. Cooperate with P7 unless new evidence suggests otherwise.
P2 cooperated when we met, strong evidence they are good. Cooperate in this final encounter to maximize mutual payoff among good players.
P1 and I mutually cooperated in round 2, supporting good status; favor C again. P6’s D against my C remains strong evidence of selfishness, though not proof.
Final round: P7 previously chose C against my C, evidence favoring a good type. Choose C to maximize good-player welfare; defect only if strong evidence P7 is selfish.
P9 chose C against my C earlier, identifying them as good under payoff-maximizing selfish play. Cooperate again to maximize good players’ total payoff.
P8 cooperated with me in round 3; reciprocate with C in the final round to support good-player welfare. P6’s D/D is evidence, not proof of selfishness; public calls for C are cheap talk.
P10, I’m sorry I defected last time despite promising C. I’ll cooperate this final round; please choose C too.
P3 cooperated with me before, strong evidence they’re good. In the final round, favor C with likely-good players; D only if selfishness seems likely.
Final encounter with P5: they cooperated against my C in round 3, so cooperate again. P6 and P7 defected against my C; these are strongest selfishness candidates.
P4 cooperated with me previously, so I’ll choose C for mutual good-player gains.
P6 defected against my C, strong evidence they are selfish despite their cooperation appeals. In this final round, defect to avoid giving a selfish player 5 points.

belief_records.strategy: Cooperate initially and update beliefs from observed actions. Favor cooperation with likely good players; defect when evidence suggests an opponent is selfish.
Cooperate initially; update beliefs from observed actions and favor cooperation with likely-good players, while protecting good-player payoff against likely-selfish players.
Cooperate initially; update beliefs from encounter behavior and favor actions that maximize expected cumulative payoff among good players.
Cooperate with likely-good opponents to maximize good players’ joint payoff; update beliefs from encounter behavior and treat claims as unverified.
Start cooperatively with an unknown opponent to support mutual gains among good players; use observed behavior to guide later actions.
Defect to maximize my payoff: it earns more than cooperation whether my opponent cooperates or defects.
Cooperate initially with an unobserved opponent; use encounter outcomes to update beliefs and adapt actions to maximize the total payoff of good players.
Cooperate with uncertain opponents to favor the total payoff of good players; update beliefs from encounter behavior.
As a good player, cooperate when the opponent is likely good to support mutual gains; defect if evidence makes a selfish opponent likely.
Cooperate with an untested opponent when they are more likely good; update beliefs and adapt from observed actions.

Cooperate with likely good players to maximize total good-player payoff; defect against likely selfish players. Treat observed cooperation as evidence of a good role and update beliefs after encounters.
Cooperate with likely-good opponents to maximize good players’ combined payoff; update identity beliefs from observed actions and adjust cooperation accordingly.
Cooperate with likely-good opponents to maximize good-player welfare; update identity beliefs from observed actions and cooperate unless evidence strongly favors a selfish opponent.
Cooperate with an unknown opponent because mutual cooperation best serves good players; update identity beliefs cautiously from observed actions and treat the leader’s promises as unverified.
Cooperate with an unknown opponent: cooperation supports greater combined gains if they are good, and P7’s cooperation is evidence they are good. Use observed actions to inform future choices.
Defect: it maximizes my immediate payoff against either opponent action.
Cooperate with likely good players; defect when evidence makes an opponent likely selfish. Update beliefs from observed actions, treating selfish players as defectors.

Cooperate because mutual cooperation or unilateral cooperation with a good player maximizes good-player payoffs; defect only when the opponent is selfish and likely to defect. Update beliefs from observed actions.
Cooperate when the opponent is more likely good; defect when evidence suggests they are selfish. P6’s defection despite promising cooperation raises my estimate that P6 is selfish.
Cooperate with an untested opponent; update role beliefs from observed actions and adapt future choices to evidence.

Cooperate with untested opponents when they are more likely good, supporting mutual gains among good players. Treat observed cooperation as evidence of a good role and update beliefs after encounters.
Cooperate with an unobserved opponent: mutual cooperation maximizes combined good-player payoff, and the chance they are good makes this preferable to defecting.
Cooperate with unobserved P2; update beliefs from encounter behavior, treating observed cooperation as evidence of a good player. Favor actions that maximize expected welfare of good players.
Cooperate with P9: mutual cooperation best serves good players at the current selfishness probability. Update from observed actions; treat public claims as unverified.
Cooperate with P8 as an unknown: mutual cooperation creates greater total payoff among good players. Treat P3 and P7’s observed cooperation as strong evidence they are good.
Defect to maximize my payoff against either possible opponent action; prior cooperation by P8 and P9 against my defection indicates they are not selfish.
Cooperate with likely-good players to maximize good-player payoffs; update identity beliefs from observed actions and treat public promises as weak evidence.
Cooperate with uncertain opponents to maximize good-player payoffs; use observed actions as evidence about objectives and reserve defection for likely selfish opponents.

Cooperate with P4 absent evidence of defection to support the good players’ total payoff. P6’s observed defection remains evidence of selfishness; P10’s cooperation modestly lowers my estimate for P10.
Defect against an untested opponent when the chance they are selfish outweighs the benefit of mutual cooperation; update beliefs from observed play.
Cooperate with untested opponents when they are more likely good, preserving mutual gains among good players; defect when evidence suggests selfishness. Update beliefs from observed actions.
Cooperate with the unobserved opponent; observed cooperation supports good-player status, and mutual cooperation maximizes good-player payoff. Continue updating beliefs from encounter actions.
Cooperate with P7 absent strong evidence they are selfish; update identity beliefs from encounter behavior and prioritize the cumulative welfare of good players.
Cooperate with P10 absent evidence of selfishness; update from encounters and treat public claims as unverified.

Cooperate with the untested P1: this supports higher combined payoff if they are good, while my current selfishness estimate is below the threshold for defecting. Update beliefs from their observed action.
Defect: it gives me a higher payoff than cooperation against either action. Prior cooperation against my defection indicates P7, P8, and P9 are not selfish.
Cooperate with P3 absent evidence of selfishness; mutual cooperation maximizes good-player payoffs, while defection is preferable only when selfishness is likely.
Cooperate with an untested opponent; this favors mutual good-player payoffs. Update identity beliefs from observed actions and defect when an opponent is likely selfish and likely to defect.
Cooperate with P8 absent evidence of defection; mutual cooperation benefits good players. P6’s observed defection remains suspicious, while P4 and P10 previously cooperated.
Cooperate with likely-good opponents to maximize good players’ total payoff; defect when an opponent is more likely selfish, since that limits losses.
Cooperate with untested opponents when mutual cooperation is likely to benefit good players; defect when evidence indicates selfishness. Update role beliefs from observed actions.

Defect against an unobserved opponent when the chance they are selfish makes protection of good players’ payoff outweigh mutual-cooperation gains. Treat observed cooperation as evidence of good status and P6’s defection as strong, but not conclusive, evidence of selfishness.
Cooperate with P6 absent evidence they are selfish; update beliefs from observed actions and prioritize the cumulative welfare of all good players.
Cooperate with P5: absent evidence of selfishness, mutual cooperation best serves good players’ joint payoff. Update identity beliefs from observed actions; treat public claims as unverified.
Cooperate with the untested P4: mutual cooperation benefits good players most, and my belief that P4 is selfish is below the threshold where defection improves expected good-player welfare.
Defect to maximize my payoff against either action; the four players who cooperated against my defection are inferred not selfish.
Cooperate with unobserved opponents unless evidence strongly suggests selfishness; treat observed cooperation as evidence of goodness and update cautiously from defections and public claims.
Cooperate with the untested opponent; this supports good-player payoffs across uncertain outcomes. Treat observed defection as evidence of selfishness and update beliefs.
Cooperate with P1 absent evidence of selfishness; mutual cooperation supports good players’ combined payoff.
Cooperate with P8, who is more likely good than selfish; update role beliefs from observed actions and continue prioritizing total payoff for good players.
Cooperate to support mutual gains among good players; update role beliefs from observed actions and treat public promises as unverified.
Cooperate with an unobserved opponent: mutual cooperation benefits both good players, and my estimated chance P4 is selfish is below the threshold for defecting. Update beliefs from observed actions.
Cooperate with unobserved P10 to favor good-player welfare; observed C is evidence of good type, while P6’s D is strong evidence of selfishness.
Cooperate with P2: mutual cooperation benefits good players, and P2 is more likely good than selfish. Update role beliefs from encounter behavior, allowing for uncertainty.
Cooperate with P9: mutual cooperation best supports good-player welfare at this selfishness estimate. Treat observed cooperation as strong evidence of a good role, and update from this encounter.
Defect to maximize my payoff against either action; P2, P3, P7, P8, and P9 cooperated against my defection, so I infer they are not selfish.
Defect when selfishness seems more likely than goodness; cooperate when a good opponent is likely, since mutual cooperation maximizes good-player payoffs.
Cooperate with the untested opponent to favor good-player payoffs; use observed defections as evidence of selfishness and cooperate with players whose observed actions support good status.

Cooperate with unobserved P5: mutual cooperation benefits good players, and there is no evidence P5 is selfish. Prioritize observed actions over claims; P6’s defection despite its cooperation message remains suspicious.
Cooperate with P3: untested players are more likely good, and mutual cooperation benefits the good players overall. Treat observed cooperation against either of my actions as evidence of a good role.
Cooperate with untested opponents to support mutual gains among good players; update role beliefs from observed actions and treat public promises as unverified.

Cooperate with P8 absent direct evidence of selfishness; mutual cooperation benefits good players, while observed cooperation supports good status. Treat P6’s defection as strong but not conclusive evidence and keep updating from actions.

Defect when the chance the opponent is selfish makes it better for good-player welfare; otherwise cooperate. Update identity beliefs from observed actions, treating cooperation as evidence of a good type.
Cooperate with P6: they are more likely good, and mutual cooperation benefits good players most. Update role beliefs from encounter actions; public promises are unverified.
Defect against an untested opponent: the chance they are selfish makes this safer for good-player welfare. Players who cooperated in our encounters are strong evidence of being good.
Defect to maximize my payoff against either action. The six players who cooperated against my defection are inferred not selfish; the remaining candidates share the residual probability.

Cooperate with an unobserved opponent absent strong evidence of selfishness; observed cooperation rules out selfishness, while defections raise suspicion. Update cautiously and maximize good-player payoffs.
Cooperate with the untested opponent to favor good-player payoffs; treat observed defections as evidence of selfishness and update beliefs.
Cooperate with P3: the available evidence makes a good opponent more likely, and mutual cooperation maximizes good players’ combined payoff.
Cooperate with P5; observed cooperation supports good roles, and mutual cooperation maximizes good-player payoffs against a likely-good opponent.

Cooperate with untested opponents when mutual cooperation is more likely to benefit good players; defect against known selfish players. Treat observed actions as role evidence and public promises as unverified.

Cooperate with unobserved P5: mutual cooperation benefits good players, and the current selfishness estimate is below the threshold where defection protects their payoff. Update beliefs from observed actions.

Choose D when the opponent is more likely selfish, otherwise C to maximize good-player welfare. Treat P6’s defection as strong evidence of selfishness and observed cooperation as evidence of goodness.
P3 and P8 are equally likely to be the one remaining selfish player; C and D have equal expected good-player payoff against P3. Choose C, and update from the encounter.
Cooperate with P2 to support mutual gains among good players; treat prior behavior as evidence, not certainty.
Defect for the higher payoff against either opponent action. Prior cooperation against my defections identifies those opponents as non-selfish; P5 and P10 remain possible.

Cooperate with unobserved P9 absent strong evidence of selfishness; observed cooperation rules out selfishness under payoff-maximizing selfish play. Treat defections as evidence, while updating cautiously.
Cooperate with the untested opponent; this favors good-player payoffs when identity is uncertain. Use observed defections as evidence of selfishness and update beliefs.

Cooperate with P7 absent evidence of selfishness; mutual cooperation best supports good players’ combined payoff. P3 and P6’s defections raise suspicion, while observed cooperation lowers suspicion of the others.
Cooperate with P6, whose selfish probability is low; treat P5’s defection as strong evidence of selfishness and update beliefs from future encounters.
Cooperate with untested P3 to support mutual gains among good players; defect against strong selfish-role candidates. Update beliefs from encounter evidence, not unverified promises.

Cooperate with P9: observed cooperation strongly supports good status, and mutual cooperation maximizes good-player welfare. P6’s defection is strong evidence of selfishness; update from the encounter.
Cooperate with unobserved P1 unless strong evidence indicates selfishness; observed cooperation is evidence of goodness, while P6’s defection against my cooperation is strong evidence of selfishness.
Cooperate with P8, who is likely good given the five known good players and three defections. Treat defections as strong but not conclusive evidence of selfishness.

The eight players I encountered all cooperated, which rules out selfishness under payoff-maximizing play. Since I am good and selfish counts are 1, 3, or 5, this leaves P6 as the only possible selfish player; defect to limit losses if P6 defects.
Defect to maximize my payoff against either possible action. The eight opponents who cooperated against my defections are not selfish; given the allowed selfish counts, I am the only selfish player.
Cooperate with unobserved P10 absent evidence of selfishness. Observed cooperation rules out selfishness under payoff-maximizing play; defections raise suspicion but are not conclusive.

Cooperate with the untested opponent: this favors good-player total payoffs unless selfishness is more likely than not. Treat observed defections as evidence of selfishness and cooperation as weaker evidence of being good.
Cooperate with unobserved P2: mutual cooperation supports good players’ combined payoff. P3 and P6 remain suspicious based on their defections; no new evidence changes my other estimates.
Cooperate with untested P7: they are more likely good than selfish, and cooperation maximizes good-player totals against a good opponent. Update beliefs from observed play.
Cooperate with P2, whose earlier cooperation supports mutual gains; defect only against strong selfish-role candidates. Update beliefs from observed actions, not unverified promises.
Cooperate with P1: our previous mutual cooperation supports good status, and mutual cooperation maximizes the combined payoff of good players.
Cooperate with P7: their past cooperation is evidence they are good, and mutual cooperation maximizes good-player welfare. P6’s defection remains strong evidence of selfishness.

Cooperate with P9, whose prior C response strongly indicates they are good; mutual cooperation maximizes good players’ joint payoff. Treat the three observed defections as strong but uncertain evidence of selfishness.
Cooperate with P8: they cooperated in our earlier encounter, and mutual cooperation maximizes good-player welfare. My observed encounters leave P6 as the only possible selfish player.
Defect for the higher payoff against either action; this is the final round, so there is no future interaction to affect.

Cooperate with P3, who cooperated before; mutual cooperation maximizes good-player payoffs. Observed cooperation strongly indicates a good player, while defections leave P2 and P6 as the remaining candidates.
Cooperate with P5 based on their prior cooperation; favor good-player total payoffs and use observed defections to update identity beliefs.
Cooperate with P4, whose earlier cooperation indicates they are good; mutual cooperation maximizes good-player welfare.
Defect against P6 after their observed defection against my cooperation; this limits losses to good players if they are selfish.
Cooperated throughout to support mutual gains among good players; treated observed defections as strong evidence of selfishness and cooperation as evidence of a good role.

Cooperated with opponents who showed cooperation and defected once against an unobserved opponent to protect good-player welfare. Updated identity beliefs from encounter actions; the repeated cooperators are good, leaving P6 as the selfish player.
